result.result:
The Pomodoro timer is built and working at 1280px and 375px. The 14 logic tests and the 4 browser tests pass, and `tsc` and `oxlint` are clean.

The logic is in `src/timer.ts` and the UI in `src/App.tsx`. Start it with `npm run dev`.

Two behaviours you didn't specify:
- **Reload mid-session:** the timer itself isn't saved, so a reload resets the current countdown to a fresh phase. The dot indicator is rebuilt from today's log, so it keeps its progress.
- **Phase changes:** each phase ends stopped, so you press Start for the next one rather than it auto-running.

## What I tested and how
- **Logic (14 tests, `npx vitest run`):** phase order with the long break after every 4th focus session, then the cycle resetting. Also pause/resume, reset, skip not counting as a session, custom durations and time formatting. The 1–90 validation rejects `0`, `91`, empty, `abc`, `2.5`, `-5` and `1e1`. Corrupt saved data falls back to defaults, and "today" is filtered by local date.
- **Browser (`npx playwright test`):** I ran the same walkthrough in real Chrome at 1280px and 375px. Playwright's fake clock lets it jump forward in time, and I checked the screenshots by eye, including the mobile break view, desktop long break and mobile invalid-input state.
  - **Display and title:** 25:00 on load, and the tab title reads "12:04 - Focus" at 12:04.
  - **Buttons and Space bar:** Start, Pause, Reset and Skip all work. Space toggles once, including when a button has focus, and does nothing while typing in a text field.
  - **Background accuracy:** a single 10-minute jump forward showed exactly 15:00 left, because the timer reads timestamps rather than counting ticks.
  - **Phases and dots:** a full focus session moves to the short break. Four sessions reach the long break with the dots at 4 of 4, and Skip works.
  - **Task label and log:** the label shows up in today's log with the finish time, and the log survives a reload (5 entries).
  - **Settings:** invalid values show an error and are never applied. Valid durations take effect at once and survive a reload.
  - **Sound:** a chime plays at the end of a phase, and the mute toggle (also saved across reloads) silences it.
  - **Layout:** there is no horizontal scroll at 375px and no page errors.
- **Not tested:** I couldn't hear the chime, only confirm the audio calls fire, and I didn't test a genuinely backgrounded tab.

One bug turned up during testing: the dot progress reset on reload, which is why it is now rebuilt from the log.

result.result:
"Long break" is now "Recharge" everywhere it appears, and the countdown digits are larger on mobile. All tests pass, and I checked both changes in Chrome at 1280px and 375px.

- **Rename:** It changed in the phase label, the Settings field, the dot caption ("4 of 4 until Recharge"), the dot indicator's accessible label, the tab title ("15:00 - Recharge") and the code comments. Internal identifiers still say `long`, and the unit test's name still mentions "long break" in parentheses.
- **Digits:** At 375px the countdown is now about 116px tall, up from 90px. I also trimmed the card padding on phones from 24px to 16px so the larger digits fit. Desktop is unchanged: the size is capped at 120px, where it was already.

What I checked:
- **Existing tests:** all 14 logic tests and the original browser walkthrough and settings tests pass at both sizes, plus `tsc` and `oxlint`. I updated the old walkthrough to expect "Recharge".
- **New browser test at both widths:**
  - The tab title reads "15:00 - Recharge" after four focus sessions.
  - The dot caption says "until Recharge".
  - No page text says "long break" any more.
  - At 375px the digit size is at least 110px.
  - The widest value, 90:00, fits inside its card with no overflow.
- **By eye:** I looked at the screenshots of mobile 90:00 and the desktop Recharge phase. Both look right, and the settings row shows "Recharge" with no clipping.

The Stats view is in. Timer and Stats tabs sit at the top, and Stats shows the 7-day chart, the week total, the streak and an Export CSV button. All 28 logic tests and all 14 browser tests pass, and `tsc` and `oxlint` are clean.

How it behaves:
- **History:** the app already kept every completed session in `localStorage`. Each session now also records its minutes, and sessions saved before this change count as 25 minutes each.
- **This week** means the last 7 days including today, the same days the chart shows.
- **Streak:** consecutive days with at least one completed session. If you haven't finished one yet today, yesterday's streak still counts until the day ends.
- **Space bar:** it starts and pauses only on the Timer tab. On Stats it does nothing, so you can't change a hidden timer by accident.
- **Export CSV:** a file named `pomodoro-sessions-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` with columns Date, Time, Task, Minutes, oldest first. It is disabled when there are no sessions. Task labels starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading `'` so spreadsheets don't read them as formulas.

I fixed one layout problem while testing. At 375px the week total ("3 h 20 min") wrapped onto two lines, so I made the stat text smaller on phones and added a check that it stays on one line.

## What I tested and how
- **Logic tests (`npx vitest run`, 14 new):**
  - **Chart days:** seven consecutive days with zeros filled in. Entries 7 days old or in the future are left out, and it holds across a daylight-saving change and the year boundary.
  - **Streak:** zero with no sessions, counting through today, still alive from yesterday, broken after a missed day, and runs longer than 7 days.
  - **CSV:** exact output, quoting of commas, quotes and newlines, formula protection, and a header-only file when empty.
  - **Other:** minute formatting and the default for old saved entries.
- **Browser tests in real Chrome at 1280px and 375px**, with a fixed clock and 8 seeded sessions across days:
  - **Tabs:** clicking and the arrow keys switch views, and the Timer view still works afterwards.
  - **Chart:** seven bars in the right order with minutes `[0,25,25,0,75,25,50]`, proportional heights and nothing clipped.
  - **Numbers:** week total 3 h 20 min, streak 3 days, 8 sessions saved, and no sideways scroll.
  - **Space bar:** pressing it on Stats leaves a running timer alone.
  - **New session:** finishing one raises the total to 225 and the last bar to 75 and adds a 9th history entry. It survives a reload and appears in the exported CSV.
  - **Export:** I read the downloaded file and compared it line by line against the expected rows, including the quoted label and the `=SUM` label.
  - **Empty state:** zeros everywhere, streak 0 and the export button disabled.
- **By eye:** I looked at the Stats screenshots at both widths and the mobile Timer view, and the earlier Timer, Settings and Recharge tests still pass.
- **Not tested:** I didn't try a real tab left open across midnight, and the Stats view doesn't refresh on its own while it stays open.
